tasks.short: Check applicants against the vacancy and pass a shortlist to the manager.

today.trigger: A batch of applications lands in Recruitee, or a recruiter asks for a clean list before a hiring day at Rotterdam, Tilburg, or Venlo.
steps: Open the vacancy and reconstruct the real requirements from the Recruitee text, the manager's Teams note, and any Word brief on SharePoint.
Read each CV and the uploaded forklift, VCA, code 95, food-safety, or driving-licence files, including phone photos.
Check site, shift pattern, language, and right-to-work signals against what that floor actually needs.
Move the Recruitee stage and write a short note for the people who seem to fit.
Mail or Teams the shortlist to the recruiter and the hiring manager, then chase missing certificates.
drudgery: Reading near-duplicate CVs for the same warehouse shift
Retyping certificate names and expiry dates into the pipeline note
Reconstructing the requirement list because it is not stored as fields
Chasing candidates who uploaded an unreadable photo of a VCA card
today.time_sinks: Most of the time goes to files that are easy yes-or-no decisions, and to vacancies where the published text and the manager's latest instruction disagree.

lenses.faster: Knock-out checks for licence, certificate, site, and shift run as soon as the application arrives, so the administrator reads the borderline files and the exceptions. Retyping certificate dates and rebuilding the requirement list drop out.
lenses.autonomous: A new Recruitee application starts a screen against that vacancy's published rules and parks a draft referral. The Monday pile-clearing reminder goes away.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would screen agency flex workers to the same bar as direct hires, and would catch an expired VCA or forklift card before someone starts a shift.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses comparing scanned cards with a checklist. The part worth keeping is the judgment on a near-miss and the short conversation with the manager about who is worth a day on the floor.
lenses.options: Each borderline file gets five dispositions: meets the rules, start once the certificate is renewed, hold for a missing document, route to a flex order, or do not proceed, each with a plain-language reason.
lenses.altitude: The administrator stops screening file by file and maintains the rule set per role family, then reviews with the recruiter which rules rejected people who would have stayed past 90 days.
reach: The recruiter's first-pass screen on standard driver and warehouse vacancies
The L&D check that a starter's Studytube-relevant certificate is valid before day one
The week-one onboarding gap list the HR business partner now chases by mail

tasks.human_edge: A person still decides whether a near-miss is worth a conversation, and can explain that call to a manager who knows the shift. A rule cannot see that a Venlo night shift will take a candidate whose Dutch is thin if the certificate and the attendance record are sound.
tasks.pattern_why: Most requirements are checkable facts, but a referral changes someone's chance of a job. The EU AI Act treats CV selection as high-risk employment use, and the works council will expect a named person to approve who is sent forward.

in_practice.trigger: A candidate applies in Recruitee, or an agency sends a proposed flex worker's papers.
steps: Load the vacancy's published knock-out rules: licence, VCA, forklift, code 95 or food safety, site, shifts, and language.
Read the CV and attachments into a scorecard with three marks only: met, not met, or unclear, and quote the evidence.
Draft a referral note that leaves out BSN and identity-document images.
The HR administrator approves or corrects the batch, including every unclear file.
Approved names move stage in Recruitee and a Teams note goes to the recruiter and the hiring manager.
in_practice.human_gate: An HR administrator approves every shortlist before anyone is referred. On office and supervisor roles the recruiter approves. Nobody is auto-rejected by a score.
systems: Studytube certificate names as the reference list
data_needed: Vacancy requirements stored as fields, not only as ad text
Application files and certificate expiry dates
Site, shift, and contract type
A labelled sample of past hires who stayed 90 days and past screen-outs
in_practice.logs_to: The Recruitee timeline and a screening log that records the rule, the evidence, and the person who approved the referral.

evidence.claim: Recruitee already supports screening questions with knockout answers and moves candidates through pipeline stages.
Phone photos of certificates and CVs written in another language are a common source of wrong expiry dates and missed names for both clerks and document models.
AI used to filter or select job applicants is high-risk employment AI under the EU AI Act, which expects human oversight, logging, and information to the person affected.

risks: A rule set that quietly rejects career-switchers or non-native Dutch speakers who would have passed probation on the floor.
A misread expiry date on a photographed VCA, forklift, or code 95 card, followed by a rejection the company cannot explain.
Turning on ranking or automated rejection without works-council consent and without a candidate notice.
BSN or a copy of an identity document leaking into a Teams shortlist or a model prompt.
research_questions: Of the last 100 warehouse and driver hires who were still here and productive at 90 days, how many would the written knock-out list have blocked?
What share of certificate files are readable PDFs with a date, and what share are phone photos or cards in another language?
Does the works council treat a new screening rule on Recruitee as a change to the personnel system that needs consent before it is used?
How many of these applications are already decided by Recruitee knockout questions, and how many are judged only from the CV?

tasks.short: Tell applicants they are hired or rejected once the decision is made.

today.trigger: A recruiter or hiring manager marks a candidate as rejected or hired, often by Teams or by moving a Recruitee stage, and expects the administrator to send the message.
steps: Find the decision and check it matches the latest stage, because mail and Recruitee sometimes disagree.
Pick a Dutch or English template from Outlook or SharePoint and fill the name, vacancy, and site.
For a hire, copy scale, hours, location, and start date from the offer note or a Word concept.
Send the mail, file any offer PDF, and deal with replies and bounce-backs.
Chase managers who said 'we will decide Friday' and then went quiet.
drudgery: Copying the same rejection into dozens of mails
Hunting the right first name and vacancy title
Waiting on a manager before a standard screen-out can be sent
Keeping a personal list of people who have not been told
today.time_sinks: The delay is rarely the typing. It is candidates sitting in 'on hold' while the administrator waits for permission to send a message whose text was already agreed.

lenses.faster: A standard rejection goes out when the recruiter sets the Recruitee reason code, using the approved Dutch or English template. Drafting, address copying, and the chase for permission disappear for that majority.
lenses.autonomous: The stage change is the trigger. A candidate who was only screened no longer waits on someone's memory or a Friday list.
lenses.ambitious: Every applicant, including people who only sent a CV and flex workers who were not chosen, would hear within one working day, with a reason the company can stand behind.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses mail-merging rejections. The conversation worth keeping is the recruiter's call to someone who spent a day on the floor and came close.
lenses.options: Five approved wordings sit behind the reason code: screened out, interviewed and not selected, internal candidate, agency candidate, and offer. The offer wording is the only one that states pay, hours, site, and start date.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the template set, the reason codes, and a weekly check that nobody has waited more than two working days, and stops being the person who presses send.
reach: The recruiter's routine rejection sending
The starter sheet the payroll specialist retypes: CAO scale, hours, site, and start date from the approved offer

tasks.human_edge: Someone has to refuse a manager's request to put a blunt or unlawful reason in writing, and has to keep internal applicants and people who came on site off the generic screen-out template. Tone and liability sit with a person.
tasks.pattern_why: The hiring decision is already recorded. A rejection is a reason code plus an approved template, which is checkable without a model. Acceptance messages stay on an exception path because they state terms the candidate will rely on.

in_practice.trigger: Recruitee stage set to rejected or to offer, with a reason code.
steps: Read the reason code, the vacancy, the language, and whether the person was interviewed.
Fill the matching template with first name, vacancy, and site only.
For an offer, insert only fields already stored on the approved offer: CAO scale, hours, location, start date, and probation.
Send standard rejections on the stage change. Hold offers, internal candidates, and any free-text case.
Log the send on the candidate timeline.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter's reason code authorises a standard rejection. The recruiter approves every acceptance message, and the administrator clears a daily queue of non-standard cases.
data_needed: Closed reason codes agreed with the recruiters
Dutch and English templates approved by HR
Offer fields structured in Recruitee
A flag for internal staff and for candidates who were interviewed
in_practice.logs_to: The Recruitee candidate timeline and the sent-mail record, kept for the recruitment retention period and no longer.

evidence.claim: Recruitee can send an email template when a candidate changes pipeline stage.
Under Dutch contract law a candidate can rely on a written statement of wage, hours, and start date once they accept it, so an offer mail is more than courtesy.
A rejection that mentions health, pregnancy, or national origin creates both an AVG problem and an equal-treatment problem; reason codes should stay factual and internal.

risks: An acceptance mail that states a scale, a start date, or a contract type the manager and the CAO did not approve.
A standard rejection sent to an internal applicant, a works-council candidate, or someone who spent a full day on site.
A reason line that reveals health data or nationality, or that disagrees with the interview notes.
Dutch-only mail to candidates whose application and floor language are not Dutch.
research_questions: What share of these messages are standard screen-outs, post-interview rejections, and offers?
What is the median number of days between the Recruitee decision and the candidate actually hearing, and what causes the wait?
Are CAO scale, hours, site, and start date fields on the Recruitee offer, or do they exist only inside a Word letter?
Which languages cover almost all candidates on warehouse and driver roles, and which templates are missing?

tasks.short: Help staff with pension, allowances, and sick-pay questions and forms.

today.trigger: An employee, a team lead, or payroll asks what someone is entitled to, or a sickness case needs papers for the arbodienst or the insurer.
steps: Identify whether the person is own staff or flex, and whether the transport CAO or the warehouse CAO applies.
Look up the contract, hours, and wage components in AFAS, then the relevant policy on SharePoint.
Answer the question on pension, shift allowance, travel, or pay during illness, often by reusing an old mail.
Collect missing enrolment details and pass them to the compensation specialist or to payroll.
For longer absence, chase dates and documents for the Wet verbetering poortwachter file while the HR business partner owns the case.
drudgery: Searching SharePoint and old mail for the last correct answer
Re-explaining the same allowance to every new shift worker
Copying contract hours into pension and enrolment forms
Chasing statutory absence dates that AFAS already holds
today.time_sinks: Two CAOs plus a changing flex population mean a large share of questions are 'which rule applies to this contract', answered from memory rather than from the contract record.

lenses.faster: The administrator asks in ordinary language and gets the contract facts from AFAS, the CAO clause, and a draft reply. Hunting last year's mail and retyping hours into a form drop out.
lenses.autonomous: A new contract in AFAS, or a sickness registration that crosses a statutory milestone, opens a checklist for the administrator. The employee no longer discovers a missing pension enrolment in month three.
lenses.ambitious: Every starter and every contract change would get a correct personal note of pension and allowances, and every long absence would show its statutory dates without a manual chase. That is the work Noordhaven does unevenly today.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses searching the handbook for a paragraph that should have been on the form. The part people value is sitting with a sick employee or a new hire who is worried about pay.
lenses.options: The same answer can be prepared as a short Teams note in plain Dutch, a letter the employee can keep, a payroll checklist of AFAS components, a flex-worker referral to the agency, or a 'do not answer, escalate to compensation and benefits' flag.
lenses.altitude: The administrator maintains the entitlement playbook by CAO and contract type, and records which questions keep returning because the handbook is unclear, instead of answering each one from scratch.
reach: The compensation specialist's first-line answers on CAO allowances and enrolment status
The payroll specialist's pre-close chase for missing pension or allowance components
The HR business partner's date checklist on a poortwachter file

tasks.human_edge: The employee often asks about a form when they are really asking whether they will be paid. Hearing that, and stopping when the CAO and the contract disagree, is the job. Wrong benefit advice is hard to take back.
tasks.pattern_why: Eligibility is full of rules, but two CAOs, agency workers, and illness under the poortwachter regime make a confident wrong sentence expensive. The administrator keeps the conversation and what is sent; the draft is prepared from the contract and the written scheme.

in_practice.trigger: An employee or manager asks an entitlement question, a starter is entered in AFAS, or an absence reaches a statutory date.
steps: Classify the person: own staff or flex, transport CAO or warehouse CAO, contract hours, site.
Pull the AFAS contract and wage components and the matching scheme text. Do not pull medical notes.
Draft the answer and the list of AFAS fields still empty.
The administrator checks the draft, sends it, or escalates to compensation and benefits or the HR business partner.
Enrolment changes and anything that alters pay go to payroll as a checked list, not as free text.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves every employee-facing answer. Compensation and benefits approves any change to a scheme, a deduction, or a pension enrolment. Medical content stays out of the draft.
data_needed: Which pension fund and allowance rules apply under each CAO
AFAS contract type, hours, scale, and components
First sick day and the company milestones already configured
A written line between Noordhaven and the three agencies on who advises flex workers
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS dossier for the enrolment or the absence milestone, with the answer stored and the medical file left where the arbodienst already keeps it.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds the contract, payroll components, and absence records that an entitlement answer has to match.
Wet verbetering poortwachter dates, including the plan van aanpak, the 42e-weeksmelding, and the first-year evaluation, can be calculated from the first sick day.

Employers covered by CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer are normally affiliated to Pensioenfonds Vervoer, while a company warehouse CAO can point somewhere else, so one enrolment script will mis-state benefits.

risks: A drafted answer that contradicts the CAO, which the employee then treats as a promise.
Enrolling an agency worker into a Noordhaven pension or allowance, or missing a part-timer who has crossed the hours threshold.
Special-category health data from an absence file pasted into Teams or a model prompt without a basis or a processor agreement.
A flex worker given Noordhaven advice on pay that the agency, as employer, actually owes, including any WAADI hirer-pay comparison.
research_questions: How many benefits questions arrive in a normal week, and which five questions account for most of them?
Which pension fund and which allowance rules apply to warehouse staff, to drivers, and to flex workers, and where is that written?
What share of this task is poortwachter paperwork versus pension and allowance administration?
Is there a processor agreement and a written ban on putting medical notes into any drafting tool?

tasks.short: Post vacancies internally and externally and tell eligible staff.

today.trigger: A hiring manager's requisition is approved, or a seasonal peak means a warehouse vacancy has to go up again on one of the three sites.
steps: Take the approved text from the recruiter, often a Word file or a long mail.
Rewrite it into Recruitee and into the house format for the intranet or a Teams post.
Post internally, then externally on the boards the recruiter names, and sometimes tell one of the three agencies.
Search AFAS by hand, or ask managers, for internal staff who might qualify.
Mail those people and answer questions about shift, site, and whether the move is a real contract.
drudgery: Pasting the same vacancy into Recruitee, Teams, and board forms
Guessing who on the other two sites should have been told
Keeping a private note of the date external posting is allowed
Closing a post that was filled and left online
today.time_sinks: The slow part is the internal-first wait and the eligible-staff list, both run from memory and diary reminders, while the external text is retyped rather than written once.

lenses.faster: One approved requisition produces the Recruitee record, the internal notice, and the channel list. Rekeying the same sentences into four places drops out.
lenses.autonomous: Approval of the requisition starts the internal posting the same day and notifies staff who match the published rules. External posting waits out the internal window without a diary reminder.
lenses.ambitious: Every qualified internal on all three sites would hear about a move that fits their certificates and shift, and every ad would be written for the floor that has to read it. Noordhaven would want more good internal moves, not more boards.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying vacancies into forms. Choosing a true angle for a hard-to-fill night shift, and talking to a colleague who might want it, is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: The same facts can be framed five ways: permanent contract after a peak, certificate paid for, internal transfer across sites, night shift with the real allowance, or a flex cover through an agency. The administrator picks one framing; the facts stay identical.
lenses.altitude: The administrator runs the posting checklist and the internal-first clock, and reviews with the recruiter which channels produced people who were still productive at 90 days.
reach: The recruiter's routine posting of a standard warehouse or driver vacancy
A draft flex order for an agency portal when the manager marks the need as peak cover rather than headcount

tasks.human_edge: Someone who knows the sites can tell when an ad written for head office will be ignored on the floor, and when 'eligible' should include a driver who wants to come off the road even though the job family does not match.
tasks.pattern_why: The requisition can be turned into postings and a staff list by rules, but the public text states pay and working time, and an internal-first period may be an OR or CAO promise. A person approves the text and the list before they go out.

in_practice.trigger: A requisition is approved in Recruitee with site, shift, contract type, and must-have certificates filled in.
steps: Draft the internal notice and the external text from the requisition fields and the approved phrasing library.
Build the eligible-staff list from AFAS: job family, site, contract, and certificates that match the published rules.
Hold external boards and agency orders until the internal window has ended.
The administrator approves the text, the list, and the channels.
Publish, notify, and take the post down when the vacancy is filled or withdrawn.
in_practice.human_gate: The HR administrator approves each public text and each internal notification list. The recruiter approves anything that states a salary range or skips the internal window.
data_needed: Structured requisition fields, including CAO scale or a salary band the recruiter has approved
The internal-first period, if the OR agreement or either CAO sets one
Employee role family, site, contract end, and certificate status
A channel list with the boards and agencies actually used
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee vacancy history, plus a short log of when the internal notice started, when external posting started, and who approved the text.

evidence.claim: Recruitee holds the vacancy record and can publish it and pass it to external job channels.
Matching internal staff on role family, location, and certificate status is a normal query on an HR core system once those fields are maintained.
The company's Power BI model refreshes from AFAS nightly, so it is a poor source for a same-day list of named employees who should be notified.

risks: A public salary or CAO scale that does not match the contract that will be offered.
External posting before an internal-first period the works council or a CAO expects.
An 'eligible staff' mail that reveals someone else's contract is ending, or that functions as a hidden performance ranking.
A direct vacancy and an agency order open for the same shift, so the role is filled twice.
research_questions: Is an internal-first period written into the works-council agreement or either CAO, and how many days is it?
Which channels produced hires who were still here at 90 days last year, and which produced applications but almost no stayers?
Can eligible internals be defined with AFAS fields alone, or do managers insist on naming people?
How often is an agency order open for the same shift as a direct vacancy?

tasks.short: Look up employee facts for a werkgeversverklaring or an official request.

today.trigger: An employee needs a werkgeversverklaring for a mortgage or lease, or a bailiff, UWV, pension fund, or lender writes to HR.
steps: Check that the requester is the employee or has a legal basis to ask.
Find the person in AFAS and, when the record is incomplete, in old mail or a SharePoint dossier.
Copy contract type, hours, start date, and the wage elements the form asks for onto a PDF or a letter.
Ask payroll when the figure is a garnishment or a component AFAS does not show cleanly.
Send the statement and keep a local copy, with varying care about what was disclosed.
drudgery: Retyping the same six contract fields onto a werkgeversverklaring
Searching shared drives for the last statement sent to the same lender
Answering chasers while the form sits half filled
Reconstructing who was allowed to receive a previous disclosure
today.time_sinks: Standard employer statements take long because the data is fetched and typed by hand. Unusual requests take long because nobody has written down what may be released.

lenses.faster: A routine employer statement pulls the AFAS fields onto the standard form. Searching personal files and retyping hours, start date, and contract type drop out.
lenses.autonomous: An employee request through a form, or a scanned bailiff letter in the HR mailbox, opens a draft statement and an authorization check the same day. The request no longer waits in a tray.
lenses.ambitious: Any employee could download a correct werkgeversverklaring on the day the lender asks, and every disclosure to a third party would have a complete AVG log. Noordhaven would want that reliability long before it wanted more statements.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping contract hours onto a PDF. The work that remains is the uncomfortable one: a deurwaarder, a worried employee, or a request that should be refused.
lenses.options: Five lawful responses are prepared: the standard werkgeversverklaring, a minimum-fields confirmation, a refusal that states what is missing, a handoff to payroll because a wage attachment is in force, and an employee self-service download.
lenses.altitude: The administrator maintains the disclosure matrix, who may receive which field and on which basis, and reviews over-shares and refusals each month instead of treating every letter as a fresh search.
reach: Payroll's extraction of employee and amount details from a beslag letter
Finance's request for an employment confirmation on a lease or credit file

tasks.human_edge: Deciding that a requester is not entitled, and refusing without handing over the rest of the file, is the part that must stay human. A wrong disclosure cannot be undone.
tasks.pattern_why: The standard statement is a fixed form filled from AFAS fields, and the allow-list of recipients can be written down. A language model is the wrong place to put a personnel file when six fields are enough.

in_practice.trigger: An employee submits a request for a werkgeversverklaring, or a bailiff, UWV, pension fund, or lender sends a named request.
steps: Match the request to an employee in AFAS and classify it: own statement, legal duty, or not entitled.
Fill only the fields that class allows: typically contract type, hours, start date, and specified wage elements.
Route wage attachments to payroll with the amount, the priority, and the debtor reference.
Release employee self-service statements from current AFAS data. Hold every third-party send for the administrator.
Store the requester, the legal basis, the fields released, and the date.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator releases every disclosure to a third party. The HR director sees any request that asks for health, disciplinary, or immigration detail. Employees can download only their own standard statement.
systems: A disclosure register in SharePoint or the AFAS dossier
data_needed: Current AFAS contract and wage elements, with a named source for each figure
A disclosure matrix agreed with HR and payroll
The incoming request and proof of identity or legal duty
A rule for how long the request and the statement are kept
in_practice.logs_to: An AVG disclosure register: who asked, what was sent, the legal basis, who approved, and when.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit stores the contract and payroll elements a Dutch employer statement needs and can generate employee documents from those fields.
Dutch mortgage lenders expect a standard werkgeversverklaring, and NHG publishes a model of that statement.
The AVG requires a legal basis and data minimisation before personnel data go to a lender, a bureau, or a finance company.

risks: Sending wage, absence, or a BSN to a lender who was entitled only to contract type and hours.
A wage attachment processed late, or processed twice because both HR and payroll keep a copy, so the employer withholds the wrong amount.
Identity documents or a full dossier placed in a mail thread or a model prompt.
A self-service statement that shows a stale scale or the wrong gross component on the morning payroll is still open.
research_questions: How many requests a month fall into werkgeversverklaring, wage attachment, UWV, pension fund, and other?
What share of employer statements can be filled from current AFAS fields with no free-text file search?
Who is allowed to approve a third-party disclosure today, and is that rule written down?
Does payroll already receive beslag letters directly, so a second HR workflow would create missed or double withholdings?

tasks.short: Compile the personnel reports that managers, the OR, and HR ask for.

today.trigger: The monthly HR meeting, an OR information request, payroll close, or a director asking for starters, leavers, and verzuim.
steps: Export staff, contracts, and absence from AFAS, and vacancies from Recruitee, often to Excel.
Add flex numbers from agency spreadsheets when someone remembers to ask for them.
Pivot headcount, starters, leavers, and absence by site and contract type.
Paste the tables into a mail, a slide, or a workbook the OR has had before.
Answer questions when the director's pack and the OR pack do not match.
drudgery: Repeating the same pivots every month
Reconciling a workbook to a Power BI page that already refreshed overnight
Chasing agency hours so flex is not missing from headcount
Reformatting one set of figures into three packs
today.time_sinks: The heavy part is cleaning exports and resolving definition fights, especially verzuim and whether flex counts, not the presentation of numbers everyone already has.

lenses.faster: The monthly pack refreshes from AFAS, Recruitee, and Studytube on a schedule: headcount, starters, leavers, verzuim, open vacancies, certificate expiries. Exporting and pivoting drop out.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly refresh and the dates of payroll close and the OR meeting trigger the pack. Nobody asks the administrator to pull the numbers.
lenses.ambitious: Site managers would get one weekly view that includes flex and own staff, and the OR, payroll, and the insurer would finally share a single verzuim definition. The company needs that consistency more than it needs more slides.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses VLOOKUP. What remains is explaining a movement the chart cannot: a wave of leavers on one shift, or a manager who does not register absence.
lenses.options: The same locked figures can be cut for the OR, the HR director, and a site manager, plus an exception list. Two scenarios sit beside the actuals: flex counted in the absence rate, and flex left out.
lenses.altitude: The administrator stops building the workbook and owns the definitions of headcount, verzuim, and flex, so Power BI, payroll, and the OR pack tie out.
reach: The people-analytics analyst's standard monthly headcount and absence pack
The controller's headcount tie-out to the payroll journal
The HR director's routine OR information tables, once the definitions are agreed

tasks.human_edge: A person has to spot a clean chart that is wrong, such as a cost-centre move that looks like forty leavers, and has to refuse a team-level sickness number that names the employee by implication. Agreeing a definition with the OR is a human act.
tasks.pattern_why: These packs are counts and lists from structured systems, and the totals can be checked against payroll. A model adds nothing to the arithmetic. A short cover note, if anyone still wants one, is written by the analyst after the figures are fixed.

in_practice.trigger: Scheduled refresh after the nightly AFAS extract, and a calendar trigger before payroll close and the OR meeting.
steps: Refresh headcount, joiners, leavers, absence hours, vacancies, and certificate expiries from the agreed sources.
Apply the locked definitions, including how flex and partial absence are treated.
Produce the exception list: unknown cost centre, missing manager, agency worker duplicated, team so small the absence figure identifies a person.
The administrator clears that list before anything goes to the OR, the insurer, or the director.
Publish the pack to the Power BI workspace and file the OR extract on SharePoint.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator signs off the exception list before an external or OR pack is sent. Internal dashboards that use the locked definitions refresh on the nightly load.
systems: Agency hour files until they are interfaced
data_needed: Written definitions of headcount, FTE, verzuim, and flex, agreed with HR, finance, and the OR
AFAS extract scope, including what it omits
Recruitee open-vacancy feed and Studytube expiry feed
A minimum group size below which absence is not shown
in_practice.logs_to: The Power BI dataset refresh history and a definition sheet on SharePoint with version and owner.

evidence.claim: Power BI already refreshes HR dashboards from a nightly AFAS extract at Noordhaven, so a hand-built monthly workbook repeats an existing feed.
AFAS Profit provides standard HR and absence reports that can be tied to payroll components.
Absence reported for a very small team can identify the sick employee, which conflicts with AVG minimisation and usually with what a works council will accept.

risks: Two verzuim formulas continuing in parallel, one in the workbook and one at the insurer, after the 'automated' pack is only a third version.
Flex workers omitted or double-counted because their hours live in agency portals and not in the nightly AFAS extract.
A team-level sickness rate that identifies a person, sent to a manager distribution list.
A cover sentence that invents a cause, such as morale or a supervisor, which the counts do not show.
research_questions: Which reports did the administrators build by hand last quarter, and which of those already exist in Power BI or AFAS?
Do the OR, the insurer, and payroll use the same absence formula, including partial days and flex?
What is the smallest team that still appears in a pack, and could a reader name the person who is ill?
Does the nightly extract include Recruitee vacancies, Studytube expiries, and agency flex, or only AFAS own staff?

tasks.short: Keep the org chart, handbook, directory, and appraisal forms current.

today.trigger: A reorganisation, a new team lead, a policy change, or a manager who cannot find the current form or the right name in the directory.
steps: Ask managers what changed, then compare that with AFAS positions and the Microsoft 365 directory.
Edit the org chart and the staff list in PowerPoint, Visio, or Excel, and mail the new version around.
Update the handbook PDF or a SharePoint page when a policy changes, sometimes without a clear version history.
Revise the performance-evaluation form when competencies or probation steps change.
Answer 'which document is the current one' for months after each update.
drudgery: Retyping names and reporting lines that AFAS already stores
Hunting the latest handbook file across SharePoint and personal drives
Merging a manager's handwritten team list with the official one
Sending 'please use this version' mails
today.time_sinks: The time sinks are version confusion and unofficial site lists. A one-line policy edit also sits for weeks because nobody is sure whether the works council has to see it first.

lenses.faster: The org chart and the directory are drafted from AFAS and the Microsoft 365 directory, and a handbook change arrives as a redline against the last approved version. Retyping names and hunting the current file drop out.
lenses.autonomous: A joiner, mover, or leaver in AFAS opens an org-chart and directory diff the next morning. Handbook pages do not change on their own.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift staff would have one current handbook they can open on a phone, and every new hire, including warehouse, would get the 90-day review on a form that matches the company's north star. Both are patchy today.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses maintaining extension lists. The argument about what a rule should say belongs to the HR director and the works council, and that argument stays.
lenses.options: A policy change is prepared as a floor card in plain Dutch, a full SharePoint article, and a 'what changed' note for team leads. The org chart is prepared by site, by shift, and with agency supervisors shown outside the Noordhaven line.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns document control: owner, version, review date, and which changes need the works council. They stop being the person who edits the PDF at midnight.
reach: The HR business partner's handbook redlines, up to the point of OR or director approval
The organisation tree the people-analytics analyst uses as a Power BI filter
The link from the 90-day form to the mandatory certificates the L&D specialist tracks in Studytube

tasks.human_edge: A person has to recognise that a small wording change is really a change to working time, appraisal, or staff data, and must go to the works council before anyone publishes it. A chart a director sketched and a chart AFAS can support are often different, and only one of them should be official.
tasks.pattern_why: Names and reporting lines can be drafted from AFAS, but a handbook or an appraisal form is something employees and the works council rely on. Publishing it has to wait for an approval, and for consent where the WOR requires it.

in_practice.trigger: An AFAS change of position or manager, a passed review date on a SharePoint policy, or an approved policy decision.
steps: Build the org-chart and directory diff from AFAS and the Microsoft 365 directory, and flag conflicts.
For a handbook or form change, produce a redline against the last version the OR and the HR director approved.
Mark whether the change touches a topic the works council must consent to, such as sickness rules, staff data, or appraisal.
The administrator confirms the diff. The HR director publishes handbook and form changes, after OR consent where it is required.
Withdraw the old file and point Teams and SharePoint at the single current version.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves directory and org-chart diffs before they are marked official. The HR director approves handbook and appraisal-form changes. Works-council consent sits in front of publication wherever the agreement or the WOR requires it.
data_needed: A complete AFAS manager and position record for all three sites and shifts
The last OR-approved version of each handbook chapter
A list of document types that require consent, maintained with the HR director
A decision on whether private mobile numbers are allowed in the directory
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history with approver and date, and a one-line consent record for any chapter that went to the works council.

evidence.claim: SharePoint stores policy documents with version history and approval before publish.
AFAS Profit maintains organisational units, positions, and the manager relationship that an org chart needs.
The Dutch works council has consent rights over a range of personnel regulations, including sickness, staff-data processing, and appraisal systems, so a silent handbook publish can be unlawful.

risks: Publishing a working-time, privacy, or appraisal change the works council has not consented to.
An official chart whose manager does not match AFAS, so the wrong person is treated as the leidinggevende for sickness and for the 90-day review.
A directory that spreads private mobile numbers or home addresses.
Two PDFs left in circulation after a partial update, with the floor using the old safety or illness rule.
research_questions: How many times last year did the handbook, the org chart, the directory, and the appraisal form each change?
Which handbook chapters have a recorded works-council consent, and which were edited in Word without it?
Is the AFAS manager field complete on night shifts at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo?
Do warehouse staff open SharePoint, or do they rely on a printed sheet and a Teams post?

role.altitude: The two HR administrators stop rekeying Recruitee, AFAS, and Word, and become the keepers of the HR checks: vacancy rules, message templates, the disclosure matrix, report definitions, and document control. Their days move to exceptions, to the accuracy of what the works council and payroll receive, and to whether a hire reaches day 90 with a valid certificate, a correct contract, and a named manager.
reach: The recruiter's first-pass screen and routine rejection messages on standard driver and warehouse roles
The payroll specialist's starter sheet, wage-attachment intake, and month-end headcount tie-out
The people-analytics analyst's standard monthly pack, once definitions are locked
The compensation specialist's first-line entitlement answers and enrolment checklists
The L&D specialist's certificate-expiry list that triggers Studytube enrolment
The HR business partner's statutory date checklist on absence files, without taking over the case conversation
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks are about a quarter of the two seats. Even if that quarter shrinks sharply, the seats do not disappear: offer terms, third-party disclosures, handbook publication, and sickness files stay with a person, and the works council has a say before staff systems and staff rules change. Flex workers who exist only in agency portals cap any AFAS-only flow. The EU AI Act caps unattended screening and ranking of candidates. Two people at this loaded cost also cannot absorb payroll calculation, dismissal advice, or the manager's poortwachter conversations.
skills_to_grow: Writing rules someone else can check: knock-out criteria, disclosure matrices, and the definitions of headcount and verzuim
Configuring Recruitee stages, AFAS fields, and SharePoint approvals instead of working around them in Excel
Practical AVG: legal basis, minimum fields, retention, and what must never enter a prompt, especially BSN and health data
Enough CAO and Wet verbetering poortwachter knowledge to see when a draft is wrong
Reading a Power BI exception list and challenging a definition with the analyst and the controller
Works-council process: which changes need consent before a personnel system or a handbook page goes live
role.ambitious_version: This role runs the hire-to-day-90 operation for three sites. Every vacancy carries structured requirements, every candidate hears within a working day, every starter has valid certificates and a correct contract in week one, every long absence shows its statutory dates, and the works council, payroll, and the HR director use one set of figures. The two administrators spend their time on the cases the rules cannot see, and on changing a rule when a 90-day leaver shows the system was wrong.
